classification.difficultyReason: Interpret north-east as a 45-degree direction, then use the resulting equal horizontal and vertical offsets to reconstruct the unmarked triangle at C. Finding its angle and converting it to a clockwise bearing requires a non-trivial geometric connection beyond the scaffolded height and area calculations.

content.prompt:
A farmer owns a paddock marked $ABCD$ in the diagram, which is located between two east–west roads. $A$ is north-east of $D$. The fence $AB$ is 1200 m, the fence $AD$ is 1500 m and the fence from $DC$ is 3200 m.

Calculate:

spec.description: Unfilled trapezoidal paddock between parallel east–west road boundaries, with vertex labels, both Road labels, Paddock label and north arrow. Decorative source blue outlines and fill are replaced by black outlines without fill.
spec.mathematics: AB and DC are parallel; A is northeast of D; D lies west of A and C lies east of B. Dimensions remain in the stem.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible; no calculated heights, offsets or bearings are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the distance between the roads, to the nearest metre

answer.worked:
Since $A$ is north-east of $D$, $AD$ makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the east–west road. Let $h$ metres be the perpendicular distance between the roads.

$$\begin{align*}h&=1500\sin45^\circ\\h&=\frac{1500}{\sqrt2}\\h&\approx1061\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the area of the paddock in hectares, to the nearest hectare

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded perpendicular height and the two parallel sides.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(1200+3200)\frac{1500}{\sqrt2}\text{ m}^2\\A&=1650000\sqrt2\text{ m}^2\\A&=165\sqrt2\text{ ha}\\A&\approx233\text{ ha}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the bearing of the corner post $B$ from the corner post $C$, correct to the nearest degree

answer.short:
$318^\circ\mathrm{T}$

Find the angle west of north, then subtract it from $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The eastward displacement from $D$ to $A$ equals the perpendicular height, $750\sqrt2$ m. Thus $B$ lies $w$ metres west and $750\sqrt2$ metres north of $C$.

$$\begin{align*}w&=3200-1200-750\sqrt2\\w&=2000-750\sqrt2\end{align*}$$

Let $\theta$ be the angle from north towards west at $C$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{2000-750\sqrt2}{750\sqrt2}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2000-750\sqrt2}{750\sqrt2}\right)\\\theta&\approx41.53^\circ\\\text{Bearing}&=360^\circ-\theta\\\text{Bearing}&\approx318^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$
